notes.meaning: God announces judgment on the ruthless conqueror, referring directly to the king of Assyria. This aggressor destroyed nations and broke treaties without any provocation. When God finishes using him, his own treachery will come back upon his head, and he will be destroyed in turn.

differ.view: Some Baptists have historically interpreted the destroyer not as ancient Assyria, but as the Roman antichrist whose oppressive power would eventually be ruined.

notes.meaning: God's people stop relying on human help and turn to the Lord in prayer. They ask Him to show mercy and give them daily strength every morning. Because their danger is constant, they look to Him for complete rescue in their time of distress.

When the Lord rises up to defend His people, the roar of His power sounds like thunder. The mixed troops from many nations in the invading army cannot stand before Him. They flee in panic as soon as God steps forward in judgment.

The enemy leaves behind vast amounts of wealth as they run away. The people of Jerusalem rush out to collect the abandoned goods. Just as swarms of hungry locusts sweep over a field and strip it clean, God's people gather all the enemy's leftover riches.

The Lord is honored and lifted up because He rules from heaven and protects His people. By overthrowing the violent invaders, He restores His city. Jerusalem is once again filled with fairness, justice, and right living before God.

True safety and steady times do not come from worldly riches or military force. God provides lasting stability through godly wisdom, knowledge, and salvation. A humble awe and respect for the Lord is the greatest treasure a nation or believer can have.

Judah falls into great fear and sorrow as the enemy approaches. Brave warriors weep out in the streets, and peace ambassadors cry bitterly because their mission failed. The Assyrian king rejected their offers and refused to make peace.

The highways are completely empty because the invading soldiers make travel too dangerous. The ruthless king broke the peace treaty even after taking payment. He shows contempt for fortified cities and cares nothing for human life.

The entire countryside suffers under the enemy's invasion. The most famous and fertile regions, including Lebanon, Sharon, Bashan, and Carmel, are stripped bare and withered. It looks as if creation itself is weeping over the terrible ruin.

When human help is gone and the crisis is at its worst, the Lord speaks. He announces that the time has come for Him to rise up and act. He will lift Himself up so that everyone sees His absolute power.

The boastful plans of the invaders will amount to nothing more than dry straw and chaff. Their plots against God's people cannot succeed. The fiery fury and pride of their own breath will turn into the very fire that destroys them.

The hostile nations will be wiped out quickly and thoroughly. They will burn away like thorns cut down and thrown into a blaze. Their destruction will be complete, like stones burned to powder in a lime kiln.

God commands all people everywhere to pay attention to His work. Both distant nations and nearby neighbors must recognize what He has done. His judgment on the oppressor is a clear display of His almighty power.

Witnessing God's fiery judgment on the enemy terrifies the hypocrites living inside Jerusalem. They realize the Lord is completely holy and deeply hates sin. Trembling with fear, they wonder how any guilty person can survive in the presence of this consuming, everlasting fire.

The prophet answers by describing the person who can safely stand before God. This person lives honestly, tells the truth, and refuses money gained by cheating or taking bribes. They guard their ears against plots of murder and refuse to look with pleasure on evil.

The person who lives this upright life will dwell safely in high places, protected like someone inside a mountain fortress. Danger cannot reach them there. God will faithfully provide them with daily food and an unfailing supply of water.

Faithful believers are promised that their humiliation will end. Instead of seeing their king in mourning clothes during a siege, they will see him in royal beauty and honor, pointing ahead to the Messiah. They will also look out over a peaceful, wide land that is no longer locked down by foreign armies.

After the danger is past, God's people will look back on their former panic with relief. They will ask what happened to the dreaded foreign officers who counted their property, weighed out the tribute, and inspected the city walls for an attack. All of those frightening enemies will be gone.

The citizens of Jerusalem will no longer have to look at the fierce foreign soldiers surrounding their walls. Those troops spoke a harsh, unfamiliar language that the people could not understand. God will remove them completely from the land.

The people are urged to look upon Jerusalem as a place of joyful worship and regular religious feasts. The city is pictured as a sturdy tent that will never be torn down or forced to move into exile. Its tent pegs will remain firmly in place, and its cords will never snap.

Jerusalem did not have a large river for defense like Nineveh or Babylon, but the Lord Himself serves as broad rivers and canals for His people. He provides all the protection and refreshment of a great waterway. Yet no enemy warship or hostile fleet will ever be able to sail on it to attack the city.

The Lord fulfills every role of good leadership for His people. He is their Judge who defends their rights, their Lawgiver who guides them, and their King who rules over them. Because He holds all supreme authority, He will surely save them.

The attacking army is compared to a disabled ship whose ropes are loose, whose mast cannot stand upright, and whose sails cannot open. Once God shatters their power, vast treasures will be left behind for the taking. The defeat is so thorough that even the lame and weak among God's people will easily carry away a share of the plunder.

In this restored community, no one will complain of physical sickness or weakness. Even better than bodily health is the deep spiritual healing God gives to His people. Everyone who lives there will have their sins completely forgiven, bringing true and lasting peace.
